::: {#cor-deviance-shift}

#### The deviance is the saturated-model deviance shifted by a constant

The [deviance](#def-deviance) of a fitted logistic regression and its [deviance relative to the saturated model](#def-saturated-deviance) differ by a constant that depends on the data and not on the fitted model:

$$
\deviance = \satdeviance - 2 \satllik.
$$

:::

::: proof
@def-deviance gives $\deviance = -2 \llikf{\hvcoef}$.
Distributing the $2$ in @eq-saturated-deviance gives $\satdeviance = 2 \satllik - 2 \llikf{\hvcoef}$.
Substituting $\deviance = -2 \llikf{\hvcoef}$ into this expression gives $\satdeviance = 2 \satllik + \deviance$.
Subtracting $2 \satllik$ from both sides gives the claim.
:::
